haiku-low.q1: The connection returning, the app coming to the foreground, or 60 seconds passing while online.
haiku-low.q3: The server detects it by comparing the change's base version with the note's current version; a mismatch is a conflict.
haiku-low.q4: N1 at version 6 holding the first phone's body, plus conflict note N2 (version 1) with the second phone's body, titled N1's title plus ' (conflict)'.
haiku-low.q5: One outbox row for that note, with the base from the first edit and the full latest body.
haiku-low.q6: Each change carries a change id; the server checks applied_changes, returns the stored result for a repeat id, and writes nothing.
haiku-low.q7: In sync_state on the phone, as the last applied seq; it is updated in the same local transaction that applies the download page.
haiku-low.q8: That page's transaction rolls back, the cursor stays put, and the same page is requested again.
haiku-low.q9: The conflict result for its change id tells it, and the outbox row is deleted. The next download applies the higher-version server note, replacing the local body.
haiku-low.q10: Only after the phone receives a result (accepted or conflict) for that change id.
haiku-low.q11: The phone keeps showing its local body and the row's base does not change; the conflict is decided when that row uploads.
haiku-low.q12: It goes into a new outbox row. If the in-flight change is accepted, the base becomes the returned version; if it conflicts, the row keeps its old base and makes its own conflict note.

sonnet.q1: The connection returning, the app coming to the foreground, or 60 seconds passing while online. No sync is tried with no network.
sonnet.q3: The server, inside the upload transaction. It compares the change's base version with the note's current version. A mismatch is a conflict.
sonnet.q4: The first phone's change is accepted: the note's version goes up (5 to 6) and it holds that phone's body. The second phone's body is saved as a new conflict note (version 1, new note id, title is the original title plus ' (conflict)'). Both writes are logged in the change log (seq 101 and 102).
sonnet.q5: One outbox row for that note, with the full latest body, the original base version (from the first edit), and one change id. It is not a diff and not several changes.
sonnet.q6: Each retry carries the same change id. The server checks applied_changes for that change id (device id plus change id, unique). If it is there, the server returns the stored result and writes nothing.
sonnet.q7: In the phone's local sync_state table, as the cursor (the last applied seq). It is updated in the same local transaction that applies the downloaded page.
sonnet.q8: The page's local transaction rolls back and the cursor stays put. The same page is requested again on the next sync, so nothing is skipped or missed.
sonnet.q9: The upload returns a conflict result saying the body was saved as a new note (N2) with its seq. The phone deletes the outbox row. On download it gets the log entries: the winning version of the original note, which it applies (the local version updates, so it shows the winner's body), and the new conflict note, which appears locally. The cursor is then saved.
sonnet.q10: Only after the phone receives a result (accepted or conflict) for that change id. A row with no result stays queued with the same change id.
sonnet.q11: If the note has an outbox row, the phone keeps showing its local body and the row's base does not change. The conflict is decided on the server when that row uploads. (The document does not say whether the local version number is updated.)
sonnet.q12: The edit goes into a new outbox row. If the in-flight change is accepted, the new row's base becomes the returned version. If the in-flight change conflicts, the new row keeps its old base and makes its own conflict note. No text is merged.
